objective: Bound complete multipart requests below the deployed platform ceiling, fully decode supported still-image bytes rather than trusting headers, generate a safe correlated server filename, preserve tenant authorization, and distinguish definite rejection from provider/database outcome uncertainty.
current_evidence: The handler trusts the browser filename extension and MIME declaration.
It reads the complete file into memory without a file-size bound.
A successful Drive upload followed by a trip_photos insert failure leaves an untracked remote object.
Vercel documents a 4.5 MB Function request-payload ceiling; the old route and UI did not state an achievable limit.
behavior_to_preserve: Authenticated active staff can upload a supported photo to an own-tenant slot.
Read-only demo, anonymous, suspended, inactive-subscription, and foreign-tenant callers remain denied by the existing authorization boundary.
Google Drive credentials and files remain tenant-scoped, and successful trip_photos records retain the existing identifiers and links.
The guide UI continues to report per-file failures without sending messages or changing customer records.
forbidden_behavior: Buffering an unbounded multipart body or forwarding an over-limit file
Accepting executable, declared-only, malformed, or mismatched image content
Using a client filename or extension in the Drive object name
Fetching tenant credentials or uploading for a foreign slot
Deleting a Drive object after an outcome-unknown insert or inviting a blind retry after provider/browser response loss
Leaving a definite rejected insert's new Drive object silently untracked
acceptance_tests: Missing authority and foreign slots cause no provider effect.
Absent/dishonest Content-Length, ignored fields, empty/oversized files, header-valid truncation, unsupported types, and MIME mismatch are bounded or rejected before credential/upload calls.
A decoded supported image is uploaded with a server-generated name and detected content type, then recorded for the verified tenant and actor.
Definite provider rejection creates no database record; response loss/5xx/malformed success is correlated and reported unknown without retry guidance.
Only a definite database rejection triggers same-token Drive deletion; transport/commit uncertainty never deletes, and cleanup uncertainty is non-retryable.
existing_customer_cases: Existing trip_photos rows and Drive files are untouched.
No migration or customer re-onboarding is required.
rollback_strategy: Source rollback only. It does not delete existing photo records or Drive files. Any failed compensation remains an explicit operational error, never an automatic historical cleanup.
